title: Capstone 13 — MCP Server with Registry and Governance

questions.question: Why does the 2026 MCP revision favor StreamableHTTP for production servers?
options: It removes the need for authentication
It is the only transport that supports tool calls
It encrypts payloads automatically
It is stateless by default, so a single endpoint behind a load balancer can scale horizontally
questions.explanation: “It is stateless by default, so a single endpoint behind a load balancer can scale horizontally” matches the lesson’s treatment of Capstone 13 — MCP Server with Registry and Governance; the alternatives conflict with its definitions or workflow.

questions.question: Which authorization model gates tool calls in this capstone?
options: OAuth 2.1 tokens carrying per-tool scopes, checked at tool-call time
A shared admin password
API keys per IP address
Mutual TLS without scopes
questions.explanation: “OAuth 2.1 tokens carrying per-tool scopes, checked at tool-call time” matches the lesson’s treatment of Capstone 13 — MCP Server with Registry and Governance; the alternatives conflict with its definitions or workflow.

questions.question: What is the role of the .well-known/mcp-capabilities document?

Holds the OPA policy bundle
Exposes the tool manifest, transport URL, and auth requirements so the registry can validate and index the server
questions.explanation: “Exposes the tool manifest, transport URL, and auth requirements so the registry can validate and index the server” matches the lesson’s treatment of Capstone 13 — MCP Server with Registry and Governance; the alternatives conflict with its definitions or workflow.

questions.question: Why do destructive tools live on a separate MCP server in this design?

They run on slower hardware
They are gated behind an approval token elevated via a Slack card within a short window
They require a different programming language
questions.explanation: “They are gated behind an approval token elevated via a Slack card within a short window” matches the lesson’s treatment of Capstone 13 — MCP Server with Registry and Governance; the alternatives conflict with its definitions or workflow.

Running everything in a single process
